hints.title: Filtering Shared Salaries
hints.text: A team requires at least two employees sharing the exact same salary value.

hints.title: Enumerating Valid Salary Categories
hints.text: Filter for salaries appearing with count >= 2, and use dense_rank ordered by salary to assign team identifiers.

hints.title: Sorting Team Members
hints.text: Order the final output by team_id ascending, then employee_id ascending.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH ValidSalaries AS (
    SELECT salary
    FROM Employees
    GROUP BY salary
    HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2
),
EligibleEmployees AS (
    SELECT
        e.employee_id,
        e.name,
        e.salary,
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY e.salary ASC) AS team_id
    FROM Employees e
    JOIN ValidSalaries v ON e.salary = v.salary
)
SELECT employee_id, name, salary, team_id
FROM EligibleEmployees
ORDER BY team_id ASC, employee_id ASC;
```

complexity.time: O(N log N) window sort over filtered salary groups
complexity.notes: Grouped frequency filtering followed by dense rank window assignment.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Self-joins can generate unwanted duplicate employee pairs.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Filtering invalid salaries first reduces the row count prior to window ranking.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should use dense_rank to assign sequential team IDs ordered by salary.
